headline: Windy, rainy storms hit today and Saturday night, with a mild, mostly dry Saturday between and more storms next week.
summary:
A strong Pacific storm system crosses western Washington today. It brings gusty south winds, mainly along the coast and in the North Interior (the northern Puget Sound and San Juan area). Gusts of 40 to 50 mph are expected, locally up to 55 mph. Wind Advisories are in effect, and the Port Townsend area was added today. Winds ease late this afternoon. Rain falls first on the coast, the Olympic Peninsula, and the north this morning, then fills in across the Seattle area this afternoon and evening. Showers taper off after midnight as the cold front moves out.

Saturday starts dry and mild, with highs in the 60s, warmer than average. A deep low pressure system then heads toward Haida Gwaii, off the north coast of British Columbia, and sends another cold front into western Washington Saturday night into Sunday. That brings more wind and rain, with the potential for strong winds along the coast. Inland areas could see gusts of 30 to 40 mph. A High Wind Watch is in place for part of the coast Saturday afternoon.

Sunday brings a brief break between systems, but attention shifts to the coast. A large train of ocean swells arrives, with seas of 20 to 25 feet offshore and a potential for high surf on the beaches. The active pattern continues next week, with more storms bringing windy weather (especially at the coast), lowland rain, and snow at high elevations, with little break. River flooding is not expected in the next seven days. But repeated rain will soak the ground and raise river levels, which could become a concern with later storms.

timeline.what: Strong frontal system with gusty south winds, especially on the coast and in the North Interior. Rain fills in across the Seattle area this afternoon and evening. Winds ease late this afternoon.
Showers taper off after midnight as the cold front exits.
Starts dry and mild after a warm front lifts north, with highs in the 60s, warmer than average. A High Wind Watch covers part of the coast Saturday afternoon.
A cold front brings another round of wind and rain. Strong winds are possible on the coast, with gusts of 30 to 40 mph inland.
Brief break between systems. A large swell train brings seas of 20 to 25 feet to the coastal waters, with potential for high surf on beaches.
More Pacific storms keep the pattern active. Each can bring wind (especially at the coast), lowland rain, and high-elevation snow, with little break.

confidence: Forecasters are fairly confident in today's wind and rain and in the active pattern continuing next week. Some details are still open: strong coastal winds Saturday night are described as a potential, high surf as a possibility, and the discussion gives no specifics on individual storms next week. River flooding is not expected in the next seven days, but forecasters note that wet soils could make later storms a concern.
hazards: Wind Advisory until 4 PM today for the Grays Harbor County coast, Island County, western Skagit and northwestern Snohomish lowlands, western Whatcom lowlands, the Port Townsend area, and San Juan County.
Wind Advisory until 1 PM today for the Northern Washington Coast.
High Wind Watch Saturday afternoon for the Grays Harbor County coast and the Northern Washington Coast.
Marine: Gale Warnings today for the coastal waters, Strait of Juan de Fuca entrances, and northern inland waters including the San Juan Islands.

Marine: Small Craft Advisories today and tonight for parts of the Strait of Juan de Fuca, Admiralty Inlet, Puget Sound and Hood Canal, and through Saturday afternoon for the Grays Harbor Bar. Rough to severe bar conditions are expected at Grays Harbor.
Marine: Gale Watches from Saturday into Sunday for the Strait of Juan de Fuca, Admiralty Inlet, the northern inland waters, and Puget Sound and Hood Canal.
Marine: Storm Watch from Saturday morning through Sunday morning for the coastal waters.

glossary.definition: The leading edge of a warmer air mass. When it passes, temperatures typically rise, as expected here on Saturday.
The leading edge of a colder air mass. It often brings a burst of rain and wind as it passes, followed by showers.
The forecasters' name for the northern inland part of western Washington, including the northern Puget Sound and San Juan Islands area.
An island group off the north coast of British Columbia. The low pressure center passes near it Saturday night, well north of Washington.
A series of long, powerful ocean waves generated by distant storms. They can create dangerous surf and rough seas at the coast.
An alert that conditions could develop that bring damaging winds, but it isn't certain yet. It is a heads-up to prepare.
Marine alerts that gale-force or storm-force winds are possible on the water. A storm is the stronger of the two.
The normal level of water in rivers between storms. Repeated rain raises base flows, so rivers have less room to absorb the next storm.
